title: Cohort-driven quarterly roadmap: priority lanes & sprint-threading for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Objective: Produce a prioritized, cohort-driven quarterly roadmap that aligns Hosted API route commitments and Model Catalog rotations to measurable OKRs, capacity constraints, and customer telemetry. Scope covers: (1) cohort segmentation (internal: orgs with heavy embeddings, external: AI-native startups + enterprise product teams); (2) prioritization lanes that map to OKRs; (3) sprint-threading guidance for cross-functional teams to land model onboarding, performance tuning, and console observability improvements within Q1 window. Out of scope: deep infra re-architecture and on-prem packaging updates (handled under separate Private deployment initiatives).

Why now: Spike in demand from two pilot enterprise accounts for deterministic latency and predictable model SLAs; telemetry shows a 22% increase in high-latency tail for chat routes when sequence length >2048. Aligning model rotations and hosted route commitments to customer cohorts reduces regression risk and clarifies capacity hedges for Dedicated sales conversations.

Success metrics (ties to OKRs): reduce cohort P99 latency by 15% for tiered hosted routes; avoid model-health regressions (no more than 2% functional regression against core evals during rotation); establish a cadence for rotating one model subset per month with automated canaries and rollback policies.

Signal sources used for prioritization: route-level latency & cost dashboards (Console), customer support tickets and CS feedback, Dedicated reservation forecasts, model eval regressions, and AB test results from last two quarters.

Outcome: A roadmap split across three lanes: "Core Stability" (SLO/regression), "Performance & Cost" (batching/quantization recommendations), and "Cohort Features" (cohort-specific enhancements like embedding-dedicated routes, cost caps). Each lane will have tagged tickets that are sprint-threaded for release windows and linked to a canary plan in the release playbook.
